meta.name: CHEM Policy Configuration
meta.description: Single source of truth for CHEM (Compositional Harm Emergence Modeling). All harm categories, visual concepts, toxic-bert label mappings, policy clauses, and tunable coefficients are defined here so that NO harm semantics are ever hardcoded inside Python files.
meta.policy_clauses_description: Maps each harm category to a numbered policy clause across real platform policy structures.

hate_speech.display_name: Hate speech targeting a person or group
hate_speech.description: Direct attacks against people on the basis of protected characteristics such as race, ethnicity, national origin, religion, caste, sexual orientation, sex, gender identity, disability or serious disease.

violent_threat.description: Statements of intent, calls or aspirations to commit violence against an individual or group, or threats that could lead to death or serious injury.

child_safety.description: Content that sexualizes, endangers, grooms, or otherwise targets minors, including attempts to establish secret contact with a child.

weapons_threat.description: Depiction or brandishing of weapons directed at a person or group in a manner that communicates intent to harm.

harassment_bullying.description: Repeated or targeted degradation, mockery, or intimidation of a private individual.

graphic_violence.description: Gratuitous depictions of violence, gore, or physical harm to people or animals.

dangerous_misinformation.description: False information that can contribute to imminent physical harm, public-health harm, or election interference.

extremist_content.description: Praise, support, or representation of dangerous organizations or individuals engaged in terrorism or organized hate.

sexual_exploitation.description: Content that sexually exploits or endangers people, including non-consensual sexual content.

coordinated_harm.description: Organized efforts by multiple actors to cause harm, brigade, or manipulate a platform.

toxic_bert_mapping.description: Maps the six unitary/toxic-bert output labels to CHEM policy harm categories. Used by the text encoder so that toxic-bert scores are re-expressed as policy categories with no hardcoded semantics in Python.

visual_concepts.description: Action-based natural-language prompts used for CLIP zero-shot classification. Harmful concepts describe a harmful action or composition, not a bare object. Safe concepts anchor the softmax so harmful scores are relative to plausible benign interpretations.

harmful.prompt: a person holding a weapon and threatening another person
a person pointing a gun at someone's head
a knife raised in a threatening manner toward a person
a person stalking or following another person with a knife in a dark place
a hooded figure holding a knife following a woman in a dark corridor
a person carrying a weapon while approaching an unsuspecting victim
a crowd of people attacking an individual
an angry mob holding torches and marching
a hate symbol such as a swastika or burning cross
graphic depiction of blood and physical injury on a person
a person physically assaulting another person
a child in a sexualized or endangered situation
an adult attempting to secretly contact a child
a person degrading or mocking another person to humiliate them
extremist propaganda imagery with flags and masked fighters
sexually explicit exploitation of a person
a fabricated news headline spreading dangerous false claims

safe.prompt: a group of friends smiling at a party
a person cooking food in a kitchen
a peaceful landscape with mountains and a lake
children playing safely in a playground
a person giving a business presentation
a pet dog sitting on a couch
a sports team celebrating a victory
a plate of food on a restaurant table

video_action_mapping.description: Maps a subset of Kinetics-400 VideoMAE action labels (substring match, case-insensitive) to CHEM harm categories. Actions not listed are treated as benign.

hate_speech.title: Hate Speech
hate_speech.text: We do not allow direct attacks against people on the basis of protected characteristics.

violent_threat.title: Violence and Incitement
violent_threat.section: I. Violence and Criminal Behavior — 1. Violence and Incitement
violent_threat.text: We remove threats of violence that could lead to death or serious injury.

child_safety.title: Child Safety
child_safety.text: Content that endangers the emotional and physical well-being of minors is prohibited.

weapons_threat.title: Restricted Goods — Weapons
weapons_threat.section: I. Violence and Criminal Behavior — 4. Coordinating Harm and Promoting Crime
weapons_threat.text: We prohibit brandishing weapons with intent to threaten or harm others.

harassment_bullying.title: Bullying and Harassment
harassment_bullying.text: We remove content that targets private individuals with degradation or intimidation.

graphic_violence.title: Violent or Graphic Content
graphic_violence.section: Violent or Dangerous Content — Graphic Content
graphic_violence.text: Gratuitous graphic depictions intended to shock are not allowed.

dangerous_misinformation.title: Systemic Risk — Disinformation
dangerous_misinformation.text: Very large platforms must mitigate dissemination of illegal or harmful disinformation.

extremist_content.title: Dangerous Organizations and Individuals
extremist_content.section: I. Violence and Criminal Behavior — 2. Dangerous Organizations
extremist_content.text: We remove praise, support, or representation of terrorist and hate organizations.

sexual_exploitation.title: Sexual Exploitation of Adults
sexual_exploitation.text: We prohibit content that sexually exploits or endangers people.

coordinated_harm.title: Mitigation of Coordinated Manipulation
coordinated_harm.text: Platforms must act against coordinated inauthentic and harmful behavior.

exculpatory_keywords.description: Words/phrases in accompanying text that signal a benign real-world context (acting, prop, costume, etc.). When any keyword matches, the image/video harm score is multiplied by exculpatory_dampening_factor before fusion.

coefficients.description: All tunable numeric coefficients. Nothing numeric that governs harm semantics is hardcoded in Python; modules read from here.
